subject: Request: Admin trace evidence for SOC 2 review
messages:
From: Emily Rhodes <emily.rhodes@helixpharma.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Admin trace evidence for SOC 2 review

Hi Irene,

We are preparing for an upcoming SOC 2 readiness assessment and the auditors asked for a sample of admin/activity traces and an explanation of the export process. Can you provide:

- A concise list of admin events and system-level actions Redwood logs (what fields are captured).
- Retention policy for admin logs vs. general audit telemetry.
- Export delivery options (file formats, signing/checksums, delivery channels).
- Any PII redaction options or filtering you can apply for a customer slice.
- Chain-of-custody / attestation your team can provide for delivered artifacts.

We also have a SIG/CAIQ question (section: administrative logging) and the auditor wants to see an example manifest for a handoff. Ideally we would get a 30–90 day contiguous sample and the manifest with checksums. Is that possible?

Requested timeline: auditors want a sample by EOD Friday (2028-12-08). Let me know what you need from our side (time windows, account IDs).

Thanks,
Emily Rhodes
Director, InfoSec – Helix Pharma
emily.rhodes@helixpharma.com
+1 415 555 0182

--
Audit contact: audit-requests@auditfirm.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rhodes <emily.rhodes@helixpharma.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-05T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Admin trace evidence for SOC 2 review

Emily — thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely provide a sample bundle and the attestation artifacts. High-level answers below; I included Kim and Ben to cover export packaging and compliance attestation if you want signatures on the manifest.

What we log (admin / operator-focused):
- Authentication and auth changes: successful/failed logins, MFA events, token issuance/revocation (token id, user id hash, timestamp).
- User & role management: create/update/delete user, role assignment, RBAC changes (actor, target, change delta).
- API key and service principal lifecycle: create, rotate, disable, delete (key id, scope).
- Console and API admin actions: model deployments, config changes (feature flags, routing policies), canary/rollout events.
- Privileged session metadata: session start/stop, source IP, user agent, elevated privilege usage.
- Data-access operator actions: exports initiated, snapshots requested, vault/unsealing events.
- System events tied to admin ops: autoscaling/deployment failures, config rollbacks.

Fields typically included: timestamp (ISO8601), actor (internal user id hashed, display where permitted), actor_email (redacted if requested), action_type, resource_type, resource_id, before/after delta (when applicable), request_id, originating_ip, user_agent, request_headers (truncated), and service node id.

Retention and scope: 
- Default audit telemetry (application logs, traces) retained 365 days.
- Admin/privileged-action ledger retained 730 days for hosted customers.
- For Redwood Dedicated / Private customers we can support custom retention windows through contract (SLA addendum).

Export and delivery options:
- Formats: CSV (manifest-friendly), newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) for event semantics, Parquet for large sets.
- Packaging: signed tar.gz bundle with per-file SHA-256 checksums and a top-level manifest.csv.
- Signing/attestation: optional HMAC-based envelope plus a compliance team GPG signature for the manifest.
- Delivery channels: pre-signed S3 URL (HTTPS), SFTP push, or secure share portal.
- Chain-of-custody: manifest + checksums + a time-stamped signing artifact; we provide a short chain-of-custody statement PDF signed by Redwood Compliance.

Redaction and scoping:
- We can exclude/ redaction: email addresses, full user identifiers, and selected request headers.
- Hashing: internal user IDs are hashed by default; we can provide a mapping table under an NDA if auditors require re-identification.

Sampling window and timeline:
- We can produce a 30–90 day contiguous sample. For EOD Friday (2028-12-08) we can deliver a 30-day sample if you confirm tenant/account identifiers and timezone preference by EOD today.

Next steps / what we need from you:
- Account ID(s) or org name to slice (Helix tenant id or example project id).
- Preferred sample window (e.g., 2028-09-01 — 2028-11-30).
- Desired level of redaction (none / redact emails / redact user_ids).

Attachments we will include in the sample bundle: manifest template, checksum file, and a redaction summary. Ben will prepare the export; Kim will provide the compliance attestation if you need a signed manifest.

Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

---
Note: Some of the heavier production telemetry (high-cardinality request headers) may be truncated in exported bundles to protect throughput and PII. If auditors require full headers we can discuss a scoped extraction under an evidence access agreement.

From: Emily Rhodes <emily.rhodes@helixpharma.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: audit-requests@auditfirm.com
Date: 2028-12-06T08:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Admin trace evidence for SOC 2 review

Thanks — that's very helpful. A couple quick clarifications before you pull the sample: 

1) Please include operator actions (console + API) and explicit token revocation events — auditors are specifically checking for evidence of credential revocation.
2) Can you provide the manifest with SHA-256 checksums and a short Chain-of-Custody statement that we can hand to the external assessor?
3) We prefer the sample window 2028-09-01 through 2028-11-30 and redaction = redact emails only (leave hashed user ids).

If you can get that to us by EOD Friday we'll route it to our assessor. Also would like a quick 30-minute screen share to walk through the bundle and the manifest on Thursday or Friday. Available windows: Thursday 2028-12-07 09:00–11:00 PT or Friday 2028-12-08 13:00–15:00 PT.

Emily

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rhodes <emily.rhodes@helixpharma.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-07T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Admin trace evidence for SOC 2 review

Emily — thanks, confirmed. We prepared the requested 2028-09-01 — 2028-11-30 sample (email redaction applied) and uploaded a signed delivery bundle to a secure share. Contents of the package:

- helix_admin_trace_sample_20280901-20281201.tar.gz (gzipped export: JSONL + manifest CSV per tenant)
- manifest_helix_admin_trace.csv (file list, row counts, start/end timestamps, file SHA-256)
- helix_admin_trace_checksums.sha256 (top-level checksums for verification)
- redaction_summary_helix.pdf (brief note on fields redacted and method)
- chain_of_custody_helix.pdf (signed by Redwood Compliance; includes generation time, staff operator, and GPG signature)

Delivery: secure share (one-time signed link) — https://secure-share.redwood.example/signed/helix-admin-trace-sample (expires 2028-12-14). We can also push to an S3 location if you provide a destination.

Attestation: the manifest is signed with our compliance GPG key and the checksums file is HMAC-enveloped. Kimberly will follow up with the manifest signature and Ben will stand up the screen-share to walk the bundle.

Screen-share: Thursday 2028-12-07 at 10:00 PT works for our team — sending a calendar invite now (10:00–10:30 PT).

If the assessor needs the raw user-id mapping we will require an NDA addendum and a documented evidence access request (we can prepare that template).

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

---
Attachment stubs: helix_admin_trace_sample_20280901-20281201.tar.gz (1.2GB), manifest_helix_admin_trace.csv (6KB), helix_admin_trace_checksums.sha256 (2KB), redaction_summary_helix.pdf (4KB)
